description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — July 29, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: QwenLM/qwen-code is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: QwenLM/qwen-code leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 24 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 24 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: QwenLM/qwen-code — 6 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 33.8 below its current daily pace, with 9 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 99 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
Kilo-Org/kilocode — No same-day commit after 181 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Treat a shared agent transcript as a deployment boundary
dailyInsight.insight: Qwen Code's fresh session-writer work makes one bounded, project-scoped call: if an ACP or daemon deployment lets more than one process resume the same persisted agent session, test the ownership and recovery boundary before enabling any concurrency feature. The project now documents an experimental writer lease that is default-off, fixed at process start, and unsafe across mixed settings or versions; its adjacent recovery work shows why the boundary matters after shutdown.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The inspected opt-in adds `experimental.sessionWriterLease` for ACP and daemon recorders, pins its value when the process starts so a settings reload cannot mix leased and legacy writers, and documents cross-process fencing. The related shutdown change adds writer-lock release and recovery work, rather than treating a process exit as proof that the next agent can safely resume the same history.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A shared transcript is more than a chat log when an agent can resume, branch, run tools, or make a follow-up decision from it. Two writers that disagree about ownership can turn a recovery path into a silent history fork. A named deployment boundary makes that risk testable instead of leaving it as an accidental property of timing.

actions.audience: Operator of Qwen Code ACP or daemon sessions with persisted histories
actions.label: Test one controlled writer hand-off
actions.instruction: In an isolated test workspace, start one session owner, force a second ACP or daemon process to request the same persisted session, then close or interrupt the first owner. Verify that the second writer is refused while ownership is live, can resume only after the first has released or recovered, and that a mixed setting or old process is drained before any opt-in rollout.

receipts.title: Gate session writer lease behind opt-in (#7894)
receipts.supports: Shows the restart-required, default-off writer-fencing setting, the ACP startup pinning that prevents per-request settings from mixing protocols, and the documented mixed-configuration limit.

receipts.title: Release managed session writer locks on shutdown (#7812)
receipts.supports: Shows public implementation, design, and test work for releasing managed writer locks and handling shutdown recovery rather than assuming a new process can safely take over a persisted session.

confidence.basis: Two fresh, directly inspected Qwen Code commits describe the same session-ownership boundary: one supplies a constrained rollout switch and the other supplies its shutdown and recovery mechanics.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are source-level Qwen Code receipts. They do not establish a release containing the feature, interoperability with every ACP client or filesystem, or that an operator's own transcript storage and backup process are safe.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if a later public test or issue shows two opted-in writers can concurrently modify one persisted session, if a shutdown leaves an unrecoverable lock, or if the documented setting semantics no longer require a process restart and coordinated rollout.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a public end-to-end two-process recovery test, release notes that declare the lease ready beyond experimental use, and evidence that mixed-version deployments receive a safer migration path.
